title: SLO: conditional routing and anomaly attribution pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Build a pipeline that attributes SLO burn to causal signals, filters noisy triggers, and conditionally routes alerts (primary escalation, secondary quiet channel, on-call deferral) based on attribution confidence and blast radius.

Context:
- Current burn-rate alerts fire frequently during transient downstream hiccups and batch-job spikes. This causes on-call fatigue and repeated escalations that do not correlate with customer-visible errors.
- We already ingest traces and metrics into our observability backend; trace hooks work exists in ENG-12047 and ENG-8291 introduced trace correlation improvements. However, we lack a lightweight attribution layer that maps burns -> top contributing services / request classes and suppresses false-positives.

Goals:
1) Reduce noisy pageing by 40% for non-customer-facing burns while keeping high-fidelity pages for customer-impacting SLO breaches.
2) Surface an "attribution card" in alert payloads (top 3 contributors with relative contribution percentages and sample trace links).
3) Route alerts conditionally: immediate page to infra on high-confidence customer-impacting burns; send to a quieter ops channel with passive notifications for low-confidence or infra-external noise.
4) Provide an audit trail for every suppression/fallthrough decision and expose it in Console incident timeline.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change the SLO definitions or thresholds.
- It does not replace full incident commander tooling or post-mortem workflows.
acceptance_criteria:
- New attribution pipeline deployed to staging that can consume burn events and return top-3 causal entities within < 30s.
- For 90% of simulated false-positive scenarios (background job spikes, ingestion lag), alerts are suppressed to quiet channel in staging.
- Alert payloads in Console include attribution card with service:percentage pairs and first-sampled trace URL.
- Conditional routing rules exist and are configurable via Console: (confidence >= 0.7 AND customer-impacting=true) -> page; (confidence < 0.7) -> quiet channel.
- Rollout plan (canary to 5% orgs, metrics evaluation) documented and approved in PR and Confluence.
- Unit and integration tests covering synthetic burn events and trace-linking are merged to main.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
1) Event enrichment: Add a lightweight enrichment lambda that listens to burn-rate alert stream (existing alert broker) and attaches recent error/latency metric histograms and top-scoring traces from trace index.
2) Attribution model: Implement a deterministic heuristic with scoring (latency/error weight, request frequency, prefix-match of route, trace error count). Do a later follow-up to replace with probabilistic ML model if needed.
3) Noise filter: Apply rules to suppress if (a) affected requests are < 0.2% of normal traffic AND (b) error budget spent is driven by long-running background jobs tagged by origin=cron.
4) Confidence score: Normalize attribution to [0,1] using heuristics; expose in payload.
5) Routing: Add routing plugin to alert broker that reads confidence and tags alerts with channel (page/quiet/email).

Trade-offs considered:
- Deterministic heuristics first to keep runtime predictable; ML-based attribution would improve accuracy but requires labeled data and introduces drift maintenance.
- Enrichment must be sub-30s to avoid delaying alerts; we accept eventual consistency and provide links to later-updated attribution in Console timeline.
- We keep suppression conservative (favoring fewer false negatives) and route to quiet channel instead of full silence to preserve visibility.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for score calculation and suppression rules.
- Synthetic injection tests: generate burn events from (i) cron-heavy workload, (ii) customer-facing frontend, (iii) downstream DB latency. Validate routing decisions.
- Staging canary: enable for 10% of orgs for 48h; collect page counts, time-to-detect, and false positive rate.
- Load test enrichment lambda up to 2000 events/min to validate latency SLAs.
- Post-deploy: dashboard that compares pages/day and mean MTTA pre/post and an automated rollback if pages do not decrease or customer-impact pages drop > 5%.

risks: Attribution quality may be poor for multi-service cascades
Suppression could hide real customer-impacting incidents if tagging is incomplete
Enrichment latency could add delay to critical pages if not carefully bounded
next_steps: Implement timeout fallback (return partial attribution and mark low confidence)
Add origin-tag whitelist as requested by SRE
Prepare canary release job and telemetry pipeline
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: (1) suppression thresholds, (2) confidence normalization formula, and (3) the fallback behaviors when trace lookup fails. Comment in PR with benchmark results from staging enrichment run.
